ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure shows the high-frequency capacitance-voltage (C-V) characteristics of a Metal/SiO2/silicon (MOS) capacitor having an area of 1 × 10^-4 cm^2. Assume that the permittivities (ε0εr) of silicon and SiO2 are 1 × 10^-12 F/cm and 3.5 × 10^-13 F/cm, respectively. What is the maximum depletion layer width in silicon?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The vertical axis of the given high-frequency C-V curve is capacitance C, and the horizontal axis is voltage V. The curve is marked by a dashed line as 7 pF at the high-capacitance plateau, and is marked by a dashed line as 1 pF at the low-capacitance plateau. Therefore, read from the figure: C_ox = C_max = 7 pF, C_min = 1 pF. Reasoning: For the high-frequency MOS capacitor at maximum depletion, the measured minimum capacitance C_min is the series result of the oxide capacitance C_ox and the maximum depletion-layer capacitance C_d,max, so 1/C_d,max = 1/C_min - 1/C_ox = 1/1 - 1/7 = 6/7 pF^-1. Therefore C_d,max = 7/6 pF = 1.167 pF = 1.167 × 10^-12 F. The maximum depletion-layer width W_max = ε_si A / C_d,max = (1 × 10^-12 F/cm)(1 × 10^-4 cm^2)/(1.167 × 10^-12 F) = 8.57 × 10^-5 cm. Converted to micrometers: 8.57 × 10^-5 cm × 10^4 μm/cm = 0.857 μm.

raw_record.question_text:
The figure shows the high-frequency capacitance-voltage (C-V) characteristics of a Metal/SiO2/silicon (MOS) capacitor having an area of 1 × 10^-4 cm^2. Assume that the permittivities (ε0εr) of silicon and SiO2 are 1 × 10^-12 F/cm and 3.5 × 10^-13 F/cm, respectively.

method.method_draft: From the graph take Cox = Cmax = 7 pF and Cmin = 1 pF. Use the series-capacitance relation to find Cd,max: 1/Cd,max = 1/Cmin - 1/Cox. Then compute Wmax = eps_si A / Cd,max using eps_si = 1e-12 F/cm and A = 1e-4 cm^2. Convert the resulting value in cm to micrometers; it should give 0.857 um.
